scope: EC3 §12.7.6.2 Tables 239–240 and the directly analogous §12.7.6.3 Tables 241–242 selection behavior, with only field-name/reference selection, Include/Exclude, IncludeNoValueFields, NoExport and omitted-versus-empty Fields entries in scope.

source_locators.table_239: EC3 Table 239, printed p.552 / physical p.567: Fields is optional; each element is either an indirect field reference or a fully qualified field-name string; both forms may be mixed. If Fields is omitted, Include/Exclude is ignored and all fields are selected except NoExport; no-value handling follows IncludeNoValueFields.
source_locators.table_240: EC3 Table 240, printed p.553 / physical p.568: bit 1 selects versus excludes the Fields entries, with descendants included in the clear branch; bit 2 includes no-V fields by name only when set; NoExport has priority over the action array and flag.
source_locators.table_241_242: EC3 Table 241/Table 242, printed p.556 / physical p.571: Fields is optional; omitted means reset all and ignore Include/Exclude. Clear selects the named fields and descendants; set spares named fields and descendants. Primary Caret #174, object 5828, physical p.571 / printed p.556, inserts that descendants are also exempt in the set branch.

feature_matrix.feature: SubmitForm Fields strings and references; descendants
feature_matrix.consumer: action::field_targets parses both variants; submission::selected_names resolves references through widgets_under and names through fully-qualified name/prefix matching.
feature_matrix.assertions: submission.rs::a_no_export_field_is_left_out_even_where_the_action_names_it and ::the_include_exclude_flag_turns_the_array_inside_out test name selection/priority. form_actions_spec_audit.rs::submit_fields_reference_selects_the_referenced_fields_descendants checks indirect nonterminal selection, descendant inclusion and omitted-Fields/all-fields positive control. action.rs::each_of_the_three_form_action_types_reaches_its_own_answer parses a mixed Name+Field array, though it does not compose the mixed array.
feature_matrix.coverage: Reference descendants and string terminal names have public consumer checks; no direct consumer assertion for string-named nonterminal descendants or a mixed-array composed result was found. No behavior mismatch is established for those routes.

feature_matrix.consumer: submission::selected_names selects first; chosen filters inherited NoExport before values/format. The source says NoExport outranks the Fields array and Include/Exclude.
feature_matrix.assertions: Direct Include/Exclude inversion test uses one named field and a second field control. NoExport test names both a normal value and a NoExport value under one action; default submission also omits NoExport.
feature_matrix.coverage: The primary precedence rule has independent named-field controls. The intersection of NoExport with IncludeNoValueFields for a no-V field lacks a dedicated assertion; the draft checks this combination.

feature_matrix.feature: SubmitForm absent Fields versus explicit empty Fields array
feature_matrix.consumer: action::field_targets maps absent and [] to the same empty Vec; SubmitForm has no presence bit. submission::selected_names treats any empty Vec as absent and selects every form field, before applying Include/Exclude.
feature_matrix.assertions: Current default-submission test covers absent Fields with Flags=0; include/exclude and IncludeNoValueFields tests cover present nonempty/absent-fields arrays, but no test compares omitted /Fields to /Fields [].
feature_matrix.coverage: Source distinguishes them. With Flags=0, omitted Fields selects all eligible fields, whereas an explicitly present empty array selects none. With Include/Exclude clear and IncludeNoValueFields set, explicit [] still selects none. Current parser/composer cannot preserve this distinction; the draft isolates it with exact xref, populated controls and a source-defined empty selection.

feature_matrix.feature: ResetForm Fields strings/references, omission and descendants
feature_matrix.consumer: action::field_targets also maps absent and [] to the same empty Vec; ViewState::reached_by_reset treats empty as reset all. Name/reference target expansion applies descendants in both flag senses.
feature_matrix.assertions: view.rs::a_reset_form_action_names_fields_to_reset_or_fields_to_spare covers omitted Fields, string name, and both Include/Exclude senses. ::a_reset_form_action_named_by_reference_reaches_the_fields_descendants exercises reference-target descendants in both branches and widget reference control. Primary #174 is directly reflected by the exclusion assertions.
feature_matrix.coverage: Existing tests prove descendant inclusion/exclusion and #174. They do not distinguish `/Fields []` from omission with Include/Exclude clear. Source says omitted resets all; a present empty include list selects none. The paired draft covers that boundary.

feature_matrix.feature: SubmitForm Include/Exclude descendant ambiguity in the set branch
feature_matrix.consumer: submission::selected_names expands both reference and name targets to terminal widgets/qualified-name descendants before applying `exclude`.
feature_matrix.assertions: The current public reference-to-parent test is in the clear/include branch only. No set-branch SubmitForm ancestor exclusion test was found. ResetForm is different: Table242 initially has an asymmetry and primary #174 explicitly adds an excluded-descendants sentence; current reset tests assert it.
feature_matrix.coverage: Do not call this a confirmed gap: §12.7.6.2 explicitly says descendants are submitted in the clear branch, while its set branch says all fields except those listed. Unlike ResetForm #174, no equivalent SubmitForm annotation was found. This could support a literal only-listed-fields interpretation, but source scope is not sufficiently explicit here to assign expected runtime behavior; leave as an interpretation question, with no draft.

related_status: No existing expected-failure entry was found for omitted-versus-empty action Fields. Existing 2038-B13 concerns inherited reset defaults during save and is unrelated to selection. The acknowledged Table 239/240/241/242 rows and ADRs are broader than this bounded check; no whole-clause certification is claimed.
